issues.display_title: Issue #520: Add Panorama Quality to Get Place List
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Add Panorama Quality to Get Place List

Changes

  • Added PanoramaQuality json.RawMessage to Models.PlaceListItem with the panorama_quality JSON and GORM column mapping.
  • Added panorama_quality to Models.PlaceListItemResponse.
  • Used json.RawMessage so database JSON reaches the API response without lossy string encoding.
  • Added the field to dynamic-field responses when explicitly requested.
  • Added the field to the normal typed response.
  • Updated nearest and global grouped queries to select the latest post's value with (array_agg(panorama_quality ORDER BY latest_post DESC))[1].
  • Preserved filtering, grouping, pagination, ordering, distance calculation, contributor limiting, encryption, and existing response fields.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go
  • src/Models/PlacesModel.go

Verification

go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Places ./src/Models

Result: Places passes; Models compiles successfully with no test files.

Commits

  • c7f5a38f — model and response plumbing.
  • be905a0a — grouped-query selection for nearest and global modes.

Problem

GET /places/list did not expose the panorama_quality value available from views_place_list. Grouped nearest and global queries also did not select the latest post's value for each location group.

Scope

  • Add panorama_quality to place-list database and response models.
  • Read it in nearest and global grouped-query modes.
  • Include it in normal responses and dynamic-field responses when requested.
  • Preserve the existing API contract outside this additive response field.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Database JSON maps without lossy conversion.
  • Nearest and global modes select the latest post's panorama quality.
  • Dynamic-field responses include it only when requested.
  • Normal responses expose it for every result.
  • Focused packages compile and tests pass.

Delivery

  • Implemented in commits c7f5a38f and be905a0a

issues.display_title: Issue #521: Fix Collection Detail Panic When Elasticsearch Counter Is Missing
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Handle Missing Elasticsearch Counters in Collection Detail

Changes

  • Added a safe fallback when Elasticsearch returns no counter document for a collection post.
  • Returned zero values for counter_view, counter_like, and counter_comment instead of indexing an empty result.
  • Preserved existing counter data when the Elasticsearch document exists.
  • Added regression tests for both missing and existing Elasticsearch counter data.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail.go
  • src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail_test.go

Verification

go test ./...

Result: all packages pass.

Problem

GET /posts/collection-detail/:sid panicked with runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 when a post existed in the collection view but its Elasticsearch counter document was missing. The handler accessed postCounts[0] without checking whether the result was empty.

Affected example:

/posts/collection-detail/XmzE7c5866606d-20260828083540-f37937bcf155

Scope

  • Guard the collection-detail counter lookup against empty Elasticsearch results.
  • Use the existing zero-counter behavior already used by other post-list endpoints.
  • Preserve the endpoint response contract and unrelated behavior.
  • Add focused regression coverage.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The collection-detail endpoint does not panic when Elasticsearch returns an empty counter result.
  • Missing counter documents produce zero view, like, and comment counters.
  • Existing Elasticsearch counter documents are returned unchanged.
  • Full Go test suite passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #522: Centralize Encoded Redis String-List Reads
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Encoded Redis String-List Reads

Summary

Reused the existing Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key) helper across all non-slim encoded string-list reads in scope. The refactor changes 59 Go files, with 68 added lines and 300 removed lines. Slim files remain untouched.

Changes

  • Replaced repeated _deactive_users_ec Redis GET, base64 decode, and JSON unmarshal blocks with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Replaced all non-slim Redis.GetDeactiveUser() calls with the generic helper, preserving the intended empty-on-cache-miss behavior.
  • Removed the package-local loadRedisStrings helper from Action/V1/Recommendations/Shared.go.
  • Removed the equivalent closure from Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go.
  • Updated recommendation and V2 post handlers to use the generic helper for deactivated-user, blocked-user, and blocked-post lists.
  • Updated Redis.ViewerSuggestionUser and Redis.ReplaceBlockedPostEC to use the package-local GetEncodedStringList call.
  • Removed imports made unused by the deleted decoding code.
  • Left Redis.GetDeactiveUser and Redis.ReplaceDeactiveUser intact because Slim handlers still use them.

Affected Packages

  • Action/V1/Bookmarks: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Broadcast: 4 files
  • Action/V1/CollectionPost: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Comments: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Hashtag: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Likes: 5 files
  • Action/V1/MentionPosts: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Notifications: 1 file
  • Action/V1/Places: 5 files
  • Action/V1/Posts: 10 files
  • Action/V1/Recommendations: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Search: 7 files
  • Action/V1/Users: 5 files
  • Action/V2/Posts: 1 file
  • Utils/Redis: 1 file

Resulting Data Flow

  1. Caller supplies a context and Redis key.
  2. GetEncodedStringList reads the value through the shared Redis client.
  3. Missing values and Redis errors return an empty slice.
  4. Valid values are base64-decoded and unmarshalled into []string.
  5. Decode or unmarshal failures return an empty slice.
  6. Callers use the returned slice in their existing exclusion filters.

No database fallback, Redis write, retry, or logging was added.

Scope Audit

The final repository scan reported:

  • 58 non-slim files referencing _deactive_users_ec.
  • 58 of those files using the centralized helper.

Verification

gofmt -l <all changed Go files>
git diff --check
go test ./...

Results:

  • All 59 changed Go files are formatted.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • go test ./... succeeds with no failing package.

Problem

Non-slim handlers repeatedly read Redis keys containing base64-encoded JSON string arrays. Each handler performed the same Redis GET, base64 decode, JSON unmarshal, and empty-value handling. The duplicated code was used most often for deactivated-user exclusions and was also copied into local helpers for blocked-user and blocked-post exclusions.

The repository already provides Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key), so maintaining separate copies adds drift without adding behavior.

Scope

  • Reuse Redis.GetEncodedStringList for every non-slim deactivated-user exclusion read.
  • Replace non-slim calls to the specialized Redis.GetDeactiveUser helper with the generic helper.
  • Remove local Redis string-list loaders when the generic helper provides the same behavior.
  • Reuse the helper for related blocked-user and blocked-post reads when they were handled by those removed local loaders.
  • Update matching Redis package internals.
  • Preserve routes, queries, response shapes, filtering rules, ordering, pagination, and encryption behavior.
  • Keep all *Slim.go files unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

Redis.GetEncodedStringList returns an empty string slice when the key is missing, Redis returns an error, the value is not valid base64, or the decoded value is not a JSON string array. It does not query the database or repopulate Redis. This matches the previous non-slim call-site behavior.

Out of Scope

  • Migrating Slim handlers.
  • Removing Redis.GetDeactiveUser or Redis.ReplaceDeactiveUser, which remain used by Slim handlers.
  • Changing Redis keys, expiration, cache refresh, or database fallback behavior.
  • Refactoring unrelated Redis access patterns.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Every non-slim file that reads _deactive_users_ec uses Redis.GetEncodedStringList or the unqualified package-local equivalent.
  • No non-slim handler retains the manual Redis/base64/JSON deactivated-user loading block.
  • No non-slim handler calls Redis.GetDeactiveUser.
  • No *Slim.go file changes.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • The complete Go test suite passes:
go test ./...

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-08-31. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #523: Centralize Blocked Redis String-List Reads
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Blocked Redis String-List Reads

Summary

Reused the existing Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key) helper for all manual non-slim blocked-user and blocked-post decoders in scope. The refactor changes 56 Go files, with 96 added lines and 602 removed lines. Slim files remain untouched.

Changes

  • Replaced 53 manual blocked-user Redis/base64/JSON decoding blocks.
  • Replaced 34 manual blocked-post Redis/base64/JSON decoding blocks.
  • Updated Redis.SuggestionUser to use the package-local shared helper for blocked users.
  • Removed unused encoding/base64 and encoding/json imports where those imports only supported the deleted blocks.
  • Removed local Redis client variables made unused by centralized reads.
  • Preserved the raw Redis existence check in Posts.ListBlockedPost; its decoded value and rebuilt value now use Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Kept the existing unused blocked-post cache read in SearchPublishedFolderBookmark while routing it through the shared helper, preserving the existing Redis interaction.

Affected Packages

  • Action/V1/Bookmarks: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Broadcast: 4 files
  • Action/V1/CollectionPost: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Comments: 6 files
  • Action/V1/Hashtag: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Likes: 4 files
  • Action/V1/MentionPosts: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Notifications: 2 files
  • Action/V1/Places: 5 files
  • Action/V1/Posts: 10 files
  • Action/V1/Search: 7 files
  • Action/V1/Users: 5 files
  • Utils/Redis: 1 file

Resulting Data Flow

  1. A handler constructs the existing blocked-user or blocked-post Redis key.
  2. GetEncodedStringList reads the value through the shared Redis client.
  3. Missing values and Redis errors return an empty []string.
  4. Valid values are base64-decoded and unmarshalled into []string.
  5. Decode or unmarshal failures return an empty []string.
  6. Existing handler logic applies the list to authorization checks or query exclusions.

No database fallback, cache write, retry, or new abstraction was added.

Scope Audit

The final repository scan reported:

  • 0 manual blocked-user decoders in non-slim code.
  • 0 manual blocked-post decoders in non-slim code.
  • 0 changed *Slim.go files.
  • 1 direct non-slim blocked-list Redis GET, intentionally retained in Posts.ListBlockedPost for missing-key detection before cache rebuild.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.

Problem

Non-slim handlers repeatedly load blocked-user and blocked-post Redis values using the same sequence: Redis GET, base64 decode, and JSON unmarshal into []string. The repository already provides Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key) for that storage format, so the duplicated decoding logic increases maintenance cost without providing different behavior.

Scope

  • Replace every manual non-slim blocked-user string-list decoder with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Replace every manual non-slim blocked-post string-list decoder with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Update the matching blocked-user read inside Utils/Redis.
  • Remove imports and local Redis client variables made unused by the refactor.
  • Preserve routes, Redis keys, query filters, response shapes, ordering, pagination, and authorization behavior.
  • Keep every *Slim.go file unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

Redis.GetEncodedStringList returns an empty []string when Redis returns an error, the key is missing, the value is empty, base64 decoding fails, or JSON unmarshalling fails. This matches the previous handlers, which ignored Redis and decoding errors and retained an empty blocked list.

Posts.ListBlockedPost is an exception in retrieval flow, not encoding format. It must retain its raw Redis lookup so it can distinguish a missing value from a present encoded empty list and call Redis.ReplaceBlockedPostEC only for the missing-value case. Decoding still uses the shared helper.

Out of Scope

  • Migrating Slim handlers.
  • Changing blocked-user or blocked-post Redis key names.
  • Changing cache expiration or refresh rules.
  • Adding database fallback, retries, logging, or new helper functions.
  • Refactoring unrelated encoded Redis values.

Acceptance Criteria

  • No manual blocked-user base64/JSON decoder remains in non-slim code.
  • No manual blocked-post base64/JSON decoder remains in non-slim code.
  • All applicable reads use Redis.GetEncodedStringList or its unqualified package-local equivalent.
  • Posts.ListBlockedPost preserves its cache-miss rebuild condition.
  • No *Slim.go file changes.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-08-31. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #524: Centralize Followings Redis String-List Reads
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Followings Redis String-List Reads

Summary

Reused the existing Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key) helper for both non-slim _list_followings_ readers. The refactor changes 2 Go files with 3 added lines and 15 removed lines. Slim files remain untouched.

Changes

  • Replaced the manual followings Redis/base64/JSON decoder in Redis.SuggestionUser with the package-local helper call.
  • Replaced the equivalent decoder in Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  • Changed the timeline followings slice from []interface{} to []string to match the Redis payload contract and the existing Redis.SuggestionUser consumer.
  • Kept the existing GORM user_id IN (?) filter unchanged.
  • Removed unused encoding/base64 and encoding/json imports from the timeline handler.
  • Removed the timeline handler's local Redis client variable after its last direct Redis read was deleted.

Affected Files

  • src/Utils/Redis/Redis.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go

Resulting Data Flow

  1. The caller constructs the existing _list_followings_ Redis key.
  2. GetEncodedStringList reads the value through the shared Redis client.
  3. Missing values and Redis errors return an empty []string.
  4. Valid values are base64-decoded and unmarshalled into []string.
  5. Decode or unmarshal failures return an empty []string.
  6. The resulting slice is used by the existing PostgreSQL exclusion or GORM IN filter.

No database fallback, Redis write, retry, logging, or new abstraction was added.

Type Compatibility

The _list_followings_ payload represents user UUIDs as JSON strings. Redis.SuggestionUser already declared the decoded data as []string and passed it through pq.Array. Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou only uses the decoded values as the arguments for user_id IN (?); GORM expands []string as query parameters in the same role previously served by []interface{}.

The change does not alter serialized API output because the followings slice is not returned to clients.

Scope Audit

The final repository scan reported:

  • 2 non-slim _list_followings_ readers using GetEncodedStringList.
  • 0 manual followings decoders in non-slim code.
  • 0 changed *Slim.go files.
  • Remaining manual followings readers exist only in excluded Slim handlers.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • Both changed Go files are formatted.

Problem

Two non-slim code paths manually read _list_followings_ Redis values using the same Redis GET, base64 decode, and JSON unmarshal sequence. The values use the same base64-encoded JSON string-array format already supported by Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, key).

Keeping separate decoders duplicates error handling and allows the expected value type to drift between callers.

Scope

  • Replace the manual _list_followings_ decoder in Redis.SuggestionUser.
  • Replace the manual _list_followings_ decoder in Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou.
  • Standardize the decoded value as []string.
  • Remove imports and local Redis client variables made unused by the refactor.
  • Preserve Redis keys, query filters, response shapes, ordering, pagination, and authorization behavior.
  • Keep every *Slim.go file unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

Redis.GetEncodedStringList returns an empty []string when Redis returns an error, the key is missing, the value is empty, base64 decoding fails, or JSON unmarshalling fails. The previous call sites ignored these errors and retained an empty slice, so failure behavior remains unchanged.

Posts.TimeLinePostJustForYou previously decoded the JSON array into []interface{}. The same Redis key was already decoded into []string by Redis.SuggestionUser, establishing that the stored values are strings. The timeline only passes the slice to GORM's IN filter, which accepts []string directly.

Out of Scope

  • Migrating Slim handlers.
  • Changing _list_followings_ writers or key names.
  • Adding Redis fallback, refresh, retry, or logging behavior.
  • Refactoring non-string Redis payloads.
  • Adding a specialized followings helper.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Both non-slim _list_followings_ readers use GetEncodedStringList.
  • No manual followings Redis/base64/JSON decoder remains in non-slim code.
  • Followings use []string in both migrated paths.
  • No *Slim.go file changes.
  • Both changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-08-31. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #525: Centralize Broadcast Optional JSON Decoding
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Broadcast Optional JSON Decoding

Summary

Added the reusable Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap utility and routed all six duplicated Broadcast post-field decoders through it. The implementation changes two handlers, the existing shared Functions file, and one focused Functions test file. No dependency was added.

Changes

  • Added exported DecodeOptionalJSONMap to src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go so other packages can reuse the same optional JSON-map decoding contract.
  • Replaced three manual decoders in ListBroadcast.
  • Replaced the same three manual decoders in ListPotdBroadcast.
  • Kept the existing caller-specific error responses:
    • Failed to unmarshal panorama quality
    • Failed to unmarshal animation filter
    • Failed to unmarshal little planet filter
  • Left the single POTD location decoder inline because it has no duplicate.
  • Moved TestDecodeOptionalJSONMap to the shared Functions package using only Go's standard testing package.

Affected Files

  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions_test.go

Resulting Data Flow

  1. A handler passes an optional database JSON string to Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap.
  2. Nil input returns (nil, nil).
  3. Non-nil input is decoded with encoding/json into map[string]interface{}.
  4. The decoded map is assigned to the existing response field.
  5. A decode error returns to the handler, which emits its unchanged field-specific HTTP response.

Tests

The focused helper test covers:

  • Nil input returning a nil map without error.
  • A valid JSON object returning its decoded value.
  • Invalid JSON returning an error.

No test framework, fixture layer, or table abstraction was added.

Scope Audit

The final scan reported:

  • 6 Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap calls across the two handlers.
  • 0 remaining direct json.Unmarshal calls for the three shared fields.
  • 0 changed Slim files.
  • 1 remaining inline optional JSON decoder for POTD location, intentionally excluded because it is not duplicated.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • The new Functions utility test passes.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.

Problem

ListBroadcast and ListPotdBroadcast each decoded the same three optional JSON fields with identical nil handling and json.Unmarshal logic:

  • panorama_quality
  • animation_filter
  • little_planet_filter

The six decoding blocks duplicated parser behavior while each caller already owned the field-specific HTTP error response.

Scope

  • Add one reusable Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap utility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go for decoding an optional JSON string into map[string]interface{}.
  • Replace all six duplicated field decoders in the two non-slim Broadcast handlers.
  • Keep field-specific HTTP error responses in each caller.
  • Preserve output maps, nil values, status codes, error messages, query behavior, ordering, and pagination.
  • Add one focused unit test for the helper.
  • Keep all Slim handlers unchanged.

Behavior Boundary

The helper must preserve the previous decoder behavior:

  • A nil pointer returns a nil map and no error.
  • A valid JSON object returns its decoded map.
  • JSON null returns a nil map and no error.
  • Invalid JSON or a non-object JSON value returns an unmarshal error.
  • Callers translate errors into their existing field-specific HTTP responses.

Out of Scope

  • Decoding the POTD location field, which has only one call site.
  • Migrating unrelated JSON decoders solely to create more callers.
  • Combining the three fields into a new model or response type.
  • Moving HTTP response construction into the parser.
  • Changing Broadcast queries or response payloads.
  • Migrating Slim handlers.
  • Adding dependencies or generic reflection-based decoding.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All six shared field decoders call Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap.
  • The decoder is available for reuse through the existing Utils/Functions package.
  • No direct decoder for the three fields remains in either handler.
  • Existing error status codes and messages remain unchanged.
  • Nil and invalid-input behavior is covered by a focused unit test.
  • No Slim file changes.
  • Changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-08-31. No commit was created.
